name: reflect
context_rationale: Reflect synthesizes slice artifacts from the current session and interactively gates on user decisions (build-checks promotion), so it depends on main-thread context.
summary: Captures learnings from the just-completed slice and updates the vault with reality across four categories: validated, corrected, discovered, and deferred. Writes reflection.json, appends to lessons-learned.json and shippability.json, optionally promotes build-checks, and auto-archives the slice. Tracks Critic calibration per TRI-1. Hands off to /commit-slice after completion.

name: reduce
context_rationale: Reduce audits the vault and code graph for structural complexity signals using file inputs and code-review-graph queries; the audit phase is mechanically runnable over file inputs with no main-thread session state required.
summary: Complexity budget enforcer that audits the vault and codebase for over-engineering, dead claims, and speculative generality against mode-specific thresholds. Produces a ranked list of reduction candidates and optionally proposes a simplification slice. Appends a post-reduction lesson to lessons-learned.json after a reduction slice ships. Can be forked as a background subagent on larger codebases.

name: drift-check
context_rationale: Drift-check compares vault files against code reality using file inputs and code-review-graph queries with no dependency on the current session's conversational state, making it fully mechanically runnable as a pre-commit hook or fresh-context subagent.
summary: Audits vault claims against code reality and flags divergence across four categories: DRIFT (blocker), UNSPECIFIED CODE (major), STALE CLAIM (major), and STALE DOC (major — a /product-doc-generated doc that no longer matches the code surface it documented, detected against the doc-manifest.json provenance anchor; skipped when no manifest exists). Runs in fast mode for pre-commit hooks or full mode for on-demand audits. Appends findings to drift-log.json via the R-32 safe channel and supports interactive --resolve mode. Designed as the detect-only, all-modes counterpart to the Heavy-mode-only /sync skill.

name: supersede-slice
context_rationale: Supersede-slice operates on named archived and active slice folders using a provided slice ID argument; the file-manipulation steps are delegable.
summary: Establishes a formal bidirectional supersession link between an archived slice whose design has been contradicted by reality and a new active slice that fixes it, per SUP-1. Appends a Supersession section to the archived reflection.json, updates the active slice's mission-brief.json frontmatter, updates _index.json to mark the archived row as superseded, and validates the link via supersede_audit.

name: archive
context_rationale: Archive operates mechanically on vault directory structure with no dependency on the current session's conversational state; it reads folder contents and regenerates index files from file inputs alone.
summary: Archives completed slices (those with reflection.json) from slices/ to slices/archive/ and regenerates both _index.json files. In normal flow /reflect auto-archives each slice; /archive handles batch cleanup and stale index rebuilds. Index regeneration is dispatched to a Haiku subagent for cost efficiency (COST-1), with the main thread owning the compare-and-swap write via vault_edit rewrite. The _index.json is kept thin: recent-10 one-liner router rows plus a pointer to action-points.json; action-points.json is never regenerated here.
